purpose: Point-in-time causal case library for significant cross-asset price moves and matched non-moves. Independent of the crypto signal engine; no trading authority.

cases.observed_move: Brent settled Sep. 15 at $108.75, up $3.07 or 2.9%, after Yanbu loadings were suspended and some Saudi European cargoes were cancelled. On Sep. 16 Reuters reported Brent down 2.7% to $105.83 as Saudi Arabia increased crude shipments via Oman; U.S. inventory evidence also reduced immediate scarcity pressure.
cases.abnormality: Two consecutive material opposite-direction daily moves around a physical supply-route shock; volatility-adjusted abnormality not yet quantified.
observed_facts: Yanbu loadings were suspended and Saudi Arabia cancelled some European cargo deliveries, contributing to Brent's Sep. 15 rise.
On Sep. 16 Saudi Arabia increased crude shipments using ship-to-ship transfers off Sohar, Oman, providing an alternative delivery route.
Brent fell despite the underlying geopolitical disruption remaining unresolved.
cases.inference: The economically relevant supply variable is effective deliverable supply after route substitution and inventory buffers, not gross capacity attached to the initially disrupted route.
cases.causal_chain: physical-route disruption -> expected deliverable-barrel shortage -> replacement/hedging demand -> price rises -> alternative routing and inventory buffers become credible -> expected net shortage falls -> scarcity premium unwinds -> crude futures fall
cases.capital_source_destination: Capital initially moved toward crude/energy scarcity exposure, then partly exited as effective supply improved; exact participant source-of-funds remains UNKNOWN.
cases.likely_marginal_buyers_sellers: Physical replacement seekers and supply-risk hedgers are plausible marginal buyers; scarcity-premium holders are plausible marginal sellers on reversal. Attribution is INFERENCE.
cases.catalyst: Yanbu disruption/cargo cancellations followed by alternative Saudi routing via Oman.
cases.transmission_mechanism: Expected effective deliverable supply changed the clearing price for near-term crude demand.
alternative_explanations: U.S. inventory news independently reduced scarcity expectations.
confirmations: Adequate inventories relative to outage duration
cases.matched_control_requirement: Compare historical port/pipeline outages with and without substitution/storage capacity.
reusable_pre_move_indicators: Net effective deliverable supply after substitution
cases.decision_support: WAIT on extrapolating crude spikes solely from headline disrupted capacity.

cases.asset: Cross-asset: U.S. rates, dollar and equities
cases.observed_move: The Fed raised the target range 25 bp to 3.75%-4.00%, but contemporaneous market reporting described markets as broadly steady rather than showing a large shock response.
cases.abnormality: High-importance macro event with muted immediate broad-market response; deliberately retained as a matched non-move/control.
observed_facts: The FOMC vote was 12-0 to raise 25 bp.
Before the decision, market pricing assigned roughly a 92% probability to a 25 bp hike.
The September SEP raised the median end-2026 policy-rate projection to 4.1% from 3.8% in June, while median 2026 GDP rose to 2.3%, unemployment fell to 4.1%, and PCE inflation rose to 3.7%.
The implementation note raised IORB to 3.90% effective Sep. 17 and retained standing repo at 4.0%.
cases.inference: The announced 25 bp hike itself contained little marginal information because it was heavily priced. The more informative policy shock was the distribution/path of future rates and the combination of stronger growth/labor projections with persistent inflation.
cases.causal_chain: pre-event expectations price near-certain hike -> Fed delivers expected hike -> little need for marginal repricing from headline action -> future-rate distribution and macro projections become the marginal information -> cross-asset prices respond mainly to surprise relative to prior path, not the sign of the policy action alone
cases.capital_source_destination: No validated large immediate reallocation attributable solely to the hike. The likely opportunity-cost channel is higher prospective cash/front-end returns versus duration/risk assets, but magnitude is UNKNOWN pending post-event flow and yield data.
cases.likely_marginal_buyers_sellers: UNKNOWN at participant level; event-driven rates/FX/equity participants likely adjusted exposures to the revised path rather than the already-priced headline hike.
cases.catalyst: September FOMC decision and Summary of Economic Projections.
cases.transmission_mechanism: Policy surprise is expectation-relative: prices change when the realized policy path differs from the distribution already embedded in yields, FX and risk assets.
alternative_explanations: Oil's same-day decline offset some hawkish inflation impulse.
Long yields had already risen materially before the meeting.
Other geopolitical and energy news contaminated the event window.
confirmations: Front-end yields and OIS reprice toward the revised path
Dollar strength persists if relative-rate advantage widens
Rate-sensitive assets weaken if real/nominal required returns remain higher
falsifiers: Rate-path markets do not retain the hawkish revision
Subsequent inflation/growth data reverse the projected path
Risk assets rise while discount rates fall because the growth revision dominates
cases.matched_control_requirement: Compare FOMC actions with similar-sized surprises but different pre-event probabilities and dot-path revisions; test headline action versus expectation-adjusted policy surprise.
reusable_pre_move_indicators: Pre-event probability distribution, not action sign
Cross-market confirmation in USD, duration and rate-sensitive equities
cases.lesson_status: SUPPORTED / PROVISIONAL / NEEDS HISTORICAL EVENT STUDY
cases.decision_support: WAIT / NO EDGE from the headline hike alone. Require expectation-adjusted path surprise plus cross-market confirmation before directional action.

cross_case_hypotheses.claim: For transport-route commodity shocks, net effective deliverable supply after substitution and inventory buffers predicts persistence better than headline gross disrupted capacity.
cross_case_hypotheses.falsification: Gross disrupted capacity predicts persistence at least as well after controlling for substitution, inventories and demand.
cross_case_hypotheses.next_test: Matched historical port/pipeline/chokepoint outages versus 1d/5d/20d returns, physical differentials and backwardation.

cross_case_hypotheses.claim: For scheduled central-bank decisions, expectation-adjusted changes in the projected policy path should explain cross-asset repricing better than the direction/sign of the announced rate action.
cross_case_hypotheses.falsification: Across timestamp-safe FOMC events, headline action direction/size explains subsequent cross-asset moves at least as well as pre-event-probability-adjusted path surprise.
cross_case_hypotheses.next_test: Build historical FOMC event sample with pre-event futures/OIS probabilities, realized action, dot/path surprise and 30m/1d/5d Treasury, USD, equity and gold responses.
